project.title: VoRD: Vocabulary of Restrictive Datasets
project.description: An RDF vocabulary for publishing operational restrictions of SPARQL services in a machine-readable form.

examples.label: Basic Service Description
examples.description: A minimal SPARQL service description with rate, result-size, and response-time restrictions.

examples.label: Exhaustive Service Description
examples.description: A comprehensive service description exercising the core VoRD restriction types and properties.

examples.label: Wikidata Rate Restrictions
examples.description: An informative example describing public Wikidata Query Service rate and processing limits.

hero.headline: Machine-readable restrictions for SPARQL services.
hero.body: VoRD extends SPARQL Service Description with explicit restriction resources for rate limits, result sizes, timeouts, quotas, concurrency, load shedding, and related HTTP signals.

resourcePanel.title: VoRD Resources
resourcePanel.body: Explore the vocabulary reference, validation schemas, implementation-oriented specification, examples, and generated ontology graph.

overviewCards.title: Describe Restrictions
overviewCards.body: Attach one or more restriction resources to an sd:Service with vord:hasRestriction and publish the operational thresholds clients need to understand.

overviewCards.title: Validate Implementations
overviewCards.body: Use the bundled SHACL and ShEx profiles to check that service descriptions expose the required VoRD links, values, scopes, and enforcement modes.

overviewCards.title: Inspect the Graph
overviewCards.body: Browse the generated relationships among restriction classes, controlled concepts, properties, and their external SPARQL, HTTP, time, and QUDT terms.

customSections.title: About VoRD
customSections.body: VoRD is designed for SPARQL endpoint maintainers and clients that need a predictable way to publish and consume operational restriction metadata.
items: Quantitative restrictions can express metrics, thresholds, units, windows, bursts, and retry hints.
Controlled SKOS concepts describe scopes and enforcement behaviors such as per-client, global, reject, throttle, and partial-result handling.
The specification defines publishing and consumption guidance for service descriptions, validation, extensions, and discovery.

footer.primary: VoRD is an RDF vocabulary for describing operational restrictions of SPARQL services.
footer.secondary: The companion site is generated from the VoRD ontology, SHACL, ShEx, examples, and specification sources.
